stories.title: U-M addiction specialist warns of kratom health risks
stories.summary: A University of Michigan addiction specialist warns that kratom products, particularly those containing synthetic opioids like 7-OH, can affect the brain similarly to fentanyl and heroin, leading to addiction. Plymouth Township has enacted its own restrictions on kratom sales, while statewide legislation remains stalled.

inputFacts.title: U-M addiction specialist warns of kratom health risks
inputFacts.summary: As Michigan House Bill 5537 remains stalled in the state Senate, some local communities are enacting their own bans on kratom sales. University of Michigan addiction specialist Eliza Hutchinson warns that synthetic opioids found in these products can lead to rapid addiction and pose significant health risks.

stories.title: Zoning can make or break small business success
stories.summary: Dexter's evolving zoning ordinances, including changes for mixed-use development and outdoor dining, have supported its local economy and small businesses. Experts suggest that municipalities should review zoning to reduce barriers for entrepreneurs, as complex regulations can hinder business establishment and growth, impacting local vitality.

inputFacts.title: Zoning can make or break small business success
inputFacts.summary: The City of Dexter has utilized strategic zoning updates over the past 50 years to foster a thriving historic downtown and commercial corridor. Experts note that flexible, form-based codes and streamlined permitting processes are essential tools for supporting small business growth and economic development.

stories.title: Faculty Senate passes vote of no confidence in UMPD and University’s handling of GEO negotiations
stories.summary: The University of Michigan Faculty Senate passed a vote of no confidence in the University's handling of Graduate Employees' Organization (GEO) negotiations and the University of Michigan Police Department (UMPD). This vote was part of a broader motion expressing solidarity with GEO and pro-Palestine activists, and criticizing the administration's response to activism.

inputFacts.title: Faculty Senate passes vote of no confidence in UMPD and University’s handling of GEO negotiations
inputFacts.summary: The University of Michigan Faculty Senate has officially passed a vote of no confidence regarding the University of Michigan Police Department and the administration's management of negotiations with the Graduate Employees' Organization. The vote reflects growing faculty dissatisfaction with institutional leadership and campus safety policies.

stories.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
stories.summary: The University of Michigan will premiere "Don't Let the Sun," an oratorio exploring the history of "sundown towns" in the U.S., including their prevalence outside the South. The work, commissioned by U-M, aims to educate audiences on this hidden dimension of American history and encourage reflection on building welcoming communities.

inputFacts.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
inputFacts.summary: A new oratorio titled 'Don't Let the Sun' explores the history of sundown towns in America. Inspired by sociologist James Loewen, the work will be performed by the U-M Chamber Choir and University Choir at Hill Auditorium on November 17.

inputFacts.title: Michigan Public's Zoe Clark discusses election fallout in Michigan
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Public's Zoe Clark spoke at an Ann Arbor/Ypsilanti Regional Chamber breakfast regarding the political landscape following the recent election. Clark discussed the potential legislative agenda for Michigan Democrats and the state's future role in presidential primaries.

inputFacts.title: YCS launches plan to combat chronic student absenteeism
inputFacts.summary: Ypsilanti Community Schools has introduced a new strategy to address chronic student absenteeism by utilizing social workers and community liaisons to provide early support to families. The district aims to tackle root causes such as poverty and health issues to improve overall student attendance.

inputFacts.title: Issues of the Environment: Townships adopt tighter fertilizer ordinances to protect the Huron River
inputFacts.summary: Several townships in Washtenaw and Livingston counties have adopted new fertilizer ordinances to reduce nutrient runoff into the Huron River watershed. These regulations include seasonal application blackouts and mandatory buffer zones near waterways to prevent harmful algal blooms and protect water quality.

inputFacts.title: Waypoint Outreach Initiative provides resources for Ypsilanti's most vulnerable residents
inputFacts.summary: The Waypoint Outreach Initiative, a new organization in Ypsilanti, is providing peer support, resource navigation, and winter outreach for residents experiencing homelessness, recovery, and reentry. Founder Brandon McDonald invites community members to connect via their Facebook page, phone, or email to access services or volunteer.

inputFacts.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: The World of Ann Arbor's Fairy Doors
inputFacts.summary: Journalist Joshua Nieman explores the origins and cultural impact of the mysterious 'fairy doors' found throughout Ann Arbor. He interviews Jonathan B. Wright, a local fairyologist who explains how the artistic movement began in his own home and expanded into the city.
